unsupported_claims: The reusable-assets entry calls the exporter 'Reusable to mint the same lever for ANY model/direction' and the summary calls the technique 'direction- and model-agnostic'. This is over-generalized. The exporter's own docstring (scripts/export_gguf_lora.py lines 14-27) shows model-specific handling: it needs the unfolded fp16 checkpoint, it must NOT apply the Hadamard to the LoRA branch, and it depends on qwen35 tensor names and on llama.cpp routing those tensors through build_lora_mm. No model other than Bonsai 2 27B was measured. The mechanism is general in principle; 'ANY model' is not evidenced.

The reading frames the source as a 'Reusable 0-USD lever: YES' without pricing the only measured path: a 27B model whose README says a CPU forward pass takes minutes, and whose MLX quantized matmul has no CUDA kernel. Nothing in the repo demonstrates a tiny/CPU lever; the lever only exists for the town after a re-derivation that no seed except 2/3 even attempts.

Key facts 5, 6, 16, 17 and 18 label 27B-base, PrismML-fork, RTX-GPU, and 9B/35B-header observations as 'this box' / 'local'. Every one of those is a belam-gpu (x86_64, RTX 2070 SUPER, 15 GiB) fact: nvidia-smi and the x86-64 fork binary cannot exist on the 4-core ARM box the town's brief names as its CPU target. The reading never separates the two boxes, so its 'local, 0-USD' claims silently assume the GPU box.

Seed 5 presents 'residual component along r falls below 1e-5 at alpha 1' as an untested falsifier, but directions/direction.json's 'verified' field already reports ~1e-6 'measured on the 2-bit pack itself', and the reading's own key_fact 9 repeats it. The residual-math half of seed 5 is already established by the source; only the behavioural transfer is open, and the reader conflates the two.

The ~1.4%-of-||W|| / 99.4%-survives claim is quoted as fact, but its only provenance is a docstring assertion in scripts/export_gguf_lora.py (lines 12-13) with no derivation or measurement in the repo; it should be tagged as a source claim, not a MEASURED number.

The 72 MiB recurrent-state figure is quoted from README.md without noting that the local node's own vram_budget.md computes the 48 SSM layers' state as '~5 MiB total'. The two sources disagree by ~14x and the reading reports only one.
errors_found: Box conflation (see unsupported_claims 3): the reading's 'local' evidence is belam-gpu, not the ARM CPU box the town is built around; seed 1's est_cost even says 'local GPU'. This is the single most consequential framing error for a CPU-first town.
Seed 5 is partly redundant: the residual-projection result it proposes to test is already stated as verified in direction.json and in the reading's own key_fact 9.
Unflagged source-internal conflict on SSM recurrent state: README.md says 72 MiB fixed; .agi/context/local-maxxing/bonsai/vram_budget.md says ~5 MiB. The reading copies README and does not reconcile.

Seeds 2 and 3 both require residual-activation capture to derive a new direction, but neither llama.cpp nor the PrismML fork exposes it, MLX/numpy/safetensors are absent from the environment, and the exporter additionally needs an unfolded fp16 checkpoint. The reading prices only 'forward passes' and not the capture harness or the unfolding step, so both seeds are cheaper on paper than in fact.

The 'qwen3.8 50b' open question was searched on HF only and declared unresolved, missing the sibling source in the same trove: bonsai2-small-gpu already establishes the Bonsai base as Qwen3.8-27B and names unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf for the MTP head. HF (checked 2026-09-20) also shows Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.8-35B-A3B and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, so '50b' is a misremember of an existing 27B/35B id, not a missing model.
Minor provenance: the reading says 477 GitHub stars; the API now returns 478 (updated_at 2026-09-20T06:58:04Z). Drift, not fabrication.
missing_angles: The per-token cost of the projection on a TINY model. The reading lists '1 dot + 1 AXPY per site' or 'two extra matmuls per site' only as an estimate, never as a fraction of a small model's total forward. For the town's target scale that overhead is proportionally large and is the first thing an efficiency-maximizing town should quantify.

Literature context: difference-in-means activation steering, representation engineering, LEACE and abliteration are established techniques. The repo's contribution is the ternary runtime projection, not the direction idea; the reading presents the technique as if its transfer to the town were novel knowledge.

The town's own dead-head/coherence-pruning thread: the reader asks whether rank-1 projection bridges to head pruning, but does not draw the load-bearing distinction — residual-stream projection removes a feature direction (capacity preserved), head pruning removes capacity. They compose (project then prune) rather than being two implementations of one equation.

Sibling-source leverage: bonsai2-small-gpu already carries the 1.5x PTQ1_0 mat-vec kernel, the MTP head graft, and the 8 GB serve line — all needed to actually run the 27B this adapter targets. The reading treats orcabonsai in isolation and so misses the obvious next-source hop.

Multimodal/VRAM angles that are directly useful to the town's tiny-on-constrained-RAM aim: the 0.858 GiB vision tower (10.7%) is a genuine memory saving when stripped, and the 0.391 GiB bias saving is disk-only unless the kernel assumes bias = -scale. The reader files both as iOS trivia.

Dual-use framing: this is a refusal-removal toolkit. The 'reusable lever' the town would import is a capability to strip safety behaviour; no use-boundary or ethics note appears anywhere in the reading.

The /lora-adapters concurrency question is left open even though the fork binary is local and could be inspected or started: upstream llama.cpp keeps LoRA scale as per-slot server state, so the 'per-request steering' premise of seed 4 may be false. A cheap read of the binary/help text (as done for --lora-init-without-apply) would have settled it.
strongest_seed: Seed 3 (generalize the runtime projection to a non-refusal behaviour — e.g. output-length/verbosity — on a tiny local model). It is the cheapest seed (ESTIMATE 1-3 CPU-hours), runs entirely on the town's target hardware, tests the single transferable idea the source actually supplies (a mean-difference direction applied as a rank-1 runtime projection), and yields a reusable behaviour-control lever for tiny models rather than re-proving a 27B GPU result. Caveat: it needs an activation-capture path the reading does not specify, so it is strongest in principle, not as written.
weakest_seed: Seed 1 (re-verify the shipped rank-1 LoRA on the local PTQ1_0 pack through the PrismML fork). It is off-aim — a 27B model on the GPU box, requiring the resident llama-server to be stopped — and the source already documents the end-to-end result (scale 0 reproduces the published refusal, scale 1 is the exact projection, scale 2 flips stubborn prompts, scale 100 destroys the model). Its marginal knowledge-per-token on CPU is near zero. Seed 5 is a close second because its residual-fraction metric is already reported as verified.
